newsitem.title: USA: HealthSouth sees deal adding $0.02-shr in 97.
newsitem.headline: HealthSouth sees deal adding $0.02-shr in 97.

text.p: HealthSouth Corp said on Tuesday its acquisition of Horizon/CMS Healthcare Corp will add between $0.01 and $0.02 per share to its 1997 earnings and enable it to earn between $2.20 and $2.30 per share in its fiscal 1998 year.
First Call analysts said they expect the company to earn $1.83 per share in 1997 and $2.23 per share in 1998.
Speaking on a conference call with investors, HealthSouth Chairman Richard Scrushy also said HealthSouth may have to divest some businesses as result of the acquisition.
He declined to specify the businesses.
He said HealthSouth still needs about six months to study the possible synergies between both companies.

"We may think there are some things that don't fit," said Scrushy, who is also the company's chief executive. He added, however, "We don't want to make any real announcements on anything like that until we complete our studies."
HealthSouth said on Tuesday it would buy Horizon/CMS in a stock swap transaction valued at about $1.6 billion, including the assumption of about $700 million in debt.

The transaction, in which HealthSouth will exchange 0.42169 of its shares for each Horizon share, creates the nation's largest network of rehabilitation facilities, with some 1,300 inpatient and outpatient facilities in all 50 states.
HealthSouth has the nation's largest network of rehabilitation facilities and Horizon the nation's second-largest network.
"We were in all 50 states but some cities we couldn't get into," said Scrushy. "This allows us to step right into those cities and lock up those (Horizon rehabilitation) contracts."
The merger would eliminate HealthSouth's most significant competitor, but the company does not expect the deal to face major regulatory challenges, Scrushy said.
As well as regulatory approval, the transaction requires Horizon/CMS shareholder approval.
Scrushy said HealthSouth approached Horizon about the transaction and had to raise its offer price because other companies were in discussions with Horizon.
Horizon officials were not available for comment.
HealthSouth shares were down 2-1/8 to 41 at midday. Horizon shares were up 2-1/8 to 16-3/8.
Scrushy said only about five percent of the combined companies' assets look to be non-strategic, although more time is needed to determine that.

He did not elaborate on the combined companies' strategy, saying only, "We expect to see a real move to HMO maganed care (in the future), and we want to look at that from a long-term point of view and make sure we do the right thing.
